questions.question: What is the difference between L2 (provider-level) prompt caching and L1 (app-level) semantic caching?
options: L2 is faster; L1 is cheaper
L2 reuses attention KV for repeated prefixes at the provider; L1 skips the LLM entirely on embedding similarity hits
L2 works for all model providers; L1 only works with OpenAI
L2 requires explicit opt-in; L1 is always enabled by default
questions.explanation: L2 (provider-level) caches the attention KV state for repeated prompt prefixes — the LLM still runs but uses cached computation. L1 (app-level) semantic caching matches incoming queries against a vector store and returns cached responses without calling the LLM at all.

questions.question: For Anthropic's Claude 3.5 Sonnet, what is the price of a cached read compared to a fresh input token?
options: $3.00/M cached vs $0.30/M fresh (10x more expensive to cache)
$0.30/M cached vs $3.00/M fresh (roughly 10x cheaper)
$1.50/M cached vs $3.00/M fresh (50% discount)
$0.30/M cached vs $0.30/M fresh (same price)
questions.explanation: Anthropic's prompt-caching rate card (2026-04): cache reads are $0.30/M vs $3.00/M for fresh input on Claude 3.5 Sonnet — roughly 10x cheaper. Advertised benefits include up to 90% cost reduction and 85% latency reduction on long prompts.

questions.question: The parallelization anti-pattern can inflate LLM bills by how much, and what causes it?
options: 2-3x inflation; parallel requests compete for the same cache slot
5-10x inflation; N parallel requests issued before the first cache write all pay full input price
1.5x inflation; parallelization adds request scheduling overhead
No inflation; the provider deduplicates parallel requests automatically
questions.explanation: When N parallel requests are issued before the first cache write completes, all N pay full input price. The lesson cites typical reports of 5-10x bill inflation from this pattern. The fix: serialize the first request, let the cache write, then parallelize.

questions.question: ProjectDiscovery improved their cache hit rate from 7% to 74%. What change achieved this?
options: Switching from OpenAI to Anthropic's caching implementation
Moving dynamic text out of the cacheable prefix
Increasing the cache TTL from 5 minutes to 1 hour
Implementing a vector similarity threshold above 0.95
questions.explanation: ProjectDiscovery (2025-11 blog) reported moving from 7% to 74% cache hit rate by restructuring prompts to move dynamic content out of the prefix. Dynamic content inside the prefix prevents cache hits because the prefix hash never matches.

questions.question: What is the typical semantic cache hit rate for open-ended chat workloads versus structured FAQ?
options: Open-ended chat: 60-70%; structured FAQ: 10-15%
Open-ended chat: 10-15%; structured FAQ: 40-70%
Both have similar hit rates of 30-40%
Neither achieves meaningful hit rates above 5%
questions.explanation: Semantic cache hit rates (community-reported production telemetry): open-ended chat ~10-15% because each query is unique; structured FAQ 40-70% because questions repeat. Voice agents repeating prompts can hit 50-80%.

questions.question: OpenAI prompt caching applies automatically for prompts above what token length?
options: 256 tokens
512 tokens
1024 tokens
2048 tokens
questions.explanation: OpenAI's prompt caching activates automatically for prompts at or above 1,024 tokens, with cached input priced at roughly 90% off the fresh input rate. No explicit configuration is required.
